subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which device uses a split-ring commutator to produce direct current as a coil rotates?
questions.explain: A dc dynamo (generator) uses a split-ring commutator, which swaps the coil's connections every half turn so the output current always flows the same way — direct current. An alternator uses slip rings and gives ac.

questions.q: Why must a transformer use an alternating current in the primary coil?
options: To create a continuously changing magnetic field that induces a p.d. in the secondary
To keep the iron core cool
questions.explain: A transformer works only with a changing magnetic field. Alternating current produces a continually changing field in the iron core, which induces an alternating p.d. in the secondary coil. A steady dc would give no induced p.d. after switch-on.

questions.q: What happens to parallel rays of light after they pass through a converging (convex) lens?
options: They spread out as if from a point behind the lens
They are absorbed by the lens
They are brought together at the principal focus
questions.explain: A converging lens refracts parallel rays so that they meet at the principal focus (focal point). A diverging lens, by contrast, spreads parallel rays out.

questions.q: What is the best tool for plotting the shape and direction of a magnetic field around a bar magnet?
questions.explain: A plotting compass needle aligns with the field at each point, letting you trace the field lines and their direction. Iron filings show the shape but not the direction.

questions.q: Which component is represented by a circle with a cross inside it?
questions.explain: A filament lamp is shown as a circle with a cross inside. A diode is a triangle pointing to a line, and a fuse is a rectangle with a line through it.

questions.q: Why does the I-V graph for a filament lamp curve (becomes less steep) as the voltage increases?
options: Current is used up in the filament
The lamp acts like a diode
Resistance increases as the filament heats up
questions.explain: As current increases the filament gets hotter, ions vibrate more and resistance increases, so current rises less steeply - giving the characteristic curve.

questions.q: What happens to the resistance of a thermistor as its temperature rises?
questions.explain: For a typical (NTC) thermistor, resistance decreases as temperature increases. This is used in temperature-sensing circuits such as thermostats.

questions.q: A converging lens brings parallel rays of light together. The point where they meet is called the:
questions.explain: A converging (convex) lens refracts parallel rays so they meet at the principal focus (focal point). The distance from the lens to this point is the focal length.

questions.q: How can you reverse the direction of the force on a wire in an electric motor?
options: It is impossible to reverse the force
By reversing either the current OR the magnetic field direction
Only by switching off the current
questions.explain: Reversing the current direction or the magnetic field direction reverses the force. (Reversing both at once returns the force to its original direction.)

questions.q: Which statement about direct current (dc) and alternating current (ac) is correct?
options: Both flow in one direction only
ac constantly reverses direction; dc is one direction
dc constantly reverses direction; ac is one direction
questions.explain: Alternating current (ac) constantly changes direction, while direct current (dc), such as from a cell or battery, flows in one direction only.

questions.q: As light intensity falling on a light-dependent resistor (LDR) increases, its resistance:
questions.explain: An LDR's resistance decreases as light intensity increases (high resistance in the dark, low resistance in bright light). This is used in light-sensing circuits.

questions.q: What is the shape of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire?
options: A field like a bar magnet
questions.explain: A current in a straight wire produces a magnetic field of concentric circles around the wire. The field is stronger nearer the wire and with a larger current.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-contact force?
questions.explain: A non-contact force acts without objects touching. Gravitational force acts at a distance; friction, air resistance and tension all require contact.

questions.q: What is the SI base unit of electric current?
questions.explain: Current is an SI base quantity and its base unit is the ampere (A). The coulomb (charge), volt (p.d.) and ohm (resistance) are derived units.

questions.q: Why is the field of a solenoid similar to that of a bar magnet?
options: Because the current flows in a circle only once
Because the wire is made of iron
Because the fields from each loop add up to give a strong uniform field inside and a bar-magnet field outside
questions.explain: The circular fields from each turn combine to give a strong, nearly uniform field inside the solenoid and an external field shaped like that of a bar magnet, with a north and south end.

questions.q: A car drives along a straight road at a steady speed. What does this tell you about the forces on it?
options: The driving force is greater than the resistive forces
The forces are balanced, giving zero resultant force
questions.explain: Steady speed in a straight line means constant velocity, so by Newton's first law the resultant force is zero — the driving force balances friction and air resistance.

questions.q: A coil rotates steadily in a magnetic field. At which position is the induced p.d. greatest?
options: When the coil is parallel to the field lines, cutting them fastest
When the coil is perpendicular to the field lines
questions.explain: The induced p.d. is largest when the coil cuts field lines at the greatest rate. This occurs as the coil moves parallel to the field lines, and is zero when it momentarily moves along the lines without cutting them.

questions.q: What are the frequency and potential difference of the UK mains supply?
questions.explain: The UK mains supply is alternating current (ac) at a frequency of 50 Hz and a potential difference of about 230 V.

questions.q: In a UK three-pin plug, what colour is the live wire?
questions.explain: The live wire is brown, the neutral wire is blue, and the earth wire is green and yellow striped. The live wire alternates between a high positive and negative potential.

questions.q: On a free-body diagram of a book resting on a table, which pair of forces is shown?
options: The weight (down) and the normal contact force from the table (up)
Only the weight of the book
questions.explain: A free-body diagram shows all forces on one object. A resting book has its weight acting downward and an equal normal contact (reaction) force from the table acting upward, so the resultant is zero.

questions.q: What did the alpha particle scattering experiment lead Rutherford to conclude?
options: Electrons orbit at fixed distances in shells
Atoms are a ball of positive charge with electrons embedded in it
Mass and positive charge are concentrated in a tiny central nucleus
questions.explain: Most alpha particles passed straight through but a few were deflected back, showing the atom is mostly empty space with a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus — replacing the plum pudding model.

questions.q: A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary coil than the primary. What does it do to the potential difference?
questions.explain: In a step-up transformer np < ns, so by Vp/Vs = np/ns the secondary (output) p.d. is greater than the primary. The current is correspondingly smaller.
